minutes.headline: Planning Board recommended water-district zoning articles 4-1 over boating/fishing concerns, and approved an ANR and a stormwater permit.
minutes.summary: The Planning Board held a combined public hearing on the marijuana bylaw and the water supply protection district bylaw and map changes, with extended debate over eliminated boating and fishing uses in Zone One and over notification of affected owners. It closed the hearing and voted recommendations on articles 26, 27 and 28, then signed decisions, approved a stormwater permit and site plan, and approved minutes. Director items covered the Howard Street comprehensive permit, a planned meeting with sewer and water bodies, and objection to the MBTA Communities information form.

public_comment.topic: Resident asked about public comment procedure; told to wait for the warrant-articles hearing.
Affected owners were not individually notified of the zone change; objected to restrictions on property rights without compensation and to farming being permitted in the protection area.
The same resident asked how the zone two line through a small part of his lot would affect it; told only the portion inside the line is regulated.

budget_items.what_was_said: A resident asked whether owners would be compensated; the board said zoning changes are not compensated and an owner could seek an assessors' abatement.
Not completing the information form could cost access to state housing choice and capital project funds; the financial impact is still being assessed with the regional planning agency.
The approved well capacity is far above the current pumped amount because of water quality.

decisions.decision: The planning director will seek the building commissioner's interpretation and an opinion from town counsel on whether boating and fishing continue as a pre-existing non-conforming use in Zone One.

The planning director will invite the select board, sewer commission, water district, town manager and conservation to a meeting on water and sewer extension down Chase Road ahead of the Howard Street project.
No pre-town-meeting meeting will be held by the board.
Board will vote recommendations on the articles that evening rather than defer to town meeting.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted 4-1 on roll call to recommend the water supply protection district revisions (article 27), with Mrs. Bertram voting no.
The board also voted 4-1 on roll call to recommend the zoning map change (article 28), again with Mrs. Bertram voting no.
After closing the hearing, the board recommended article 26, the non-medical marijuana bylaw; the ayes were heard and a roll call was recorded.
The board approved a stormwater permit and site plan for PSG Realty at 133 Leominster Shirley Road, with Mr. Brenner abstaining.
The planning director will ask the building commissioner and town counsel whether boating and fishing continue in Zone One as a pre-existing non-conforming use.

why_it_matters: Articles 26, 27 and 28 now go to Town Meeting with the board's recommendation, so residents will be asked to vote on the water-district rules and the map change that restrict how land inside the protection zones can be used.

A resident at the hearing said affected owners were not individually notified of the zone change, and the board said zoning changes carry no compensation; an owner's route is an assessors' abatement request.
Whether boating and fishing in Zone One may continue is still open, and it depends on opinions the planning director has yet to obtain.
watch_next: The building commissioner's interpretation and town counsel's opinion on boating and fishing as a pre-existing non-conforming use in Zone One.
The meeting the planning director will organize on water and sewer extension down Chase Road, ahead of the Howard Street project.
